title: Pocklington Lancaster Memorial
crew_summary: 5 killed (2 survived injured); 2 civilians also killed; pilot Plt Off. Joseph Watson Thompson, DFM
memorial_type: Memorial bench and crash site marker
narrative: Lancaster ED393 of 50 Squadron departed Skellingthorpe on the night of 26 November 1943, bound for Berlin. Diverted to Melbourne airfield near Pocklington due to thick fog, the aircraft subsequently crashed when Pilot Officer Joseph Watson Thompson lost control on takeoff — the Lancaster stalled, inverted, and came down at Pocklington in the East Riding of Yorkshire. Thompson, holder of the Distinguished Flying Medal and aged just 20, was among five crew members killed; two further crew survived with injuries, and two civilians on the ground also lost their lives. The dead included Navigator Flight Sergeant Stanley Chapman, aged 22, Bomb Aimer Flight Sergeant John Ralph Conlon, aged 21, and Flight Engineer Sergeant Reginald Walter Laws, aged 20.
cause_of_loss: Pilot lost control on takeoff; aircraft stalled, inverted and crashed
memorial_details:
Name: Avro Lancaster ED393
Type: Stone of remembrance
Description: Large piece of rough-cut limestone with one finished, diagonal face, into which a circular, black, slate tablet is inset. The dedication is depicted in raised, white capital letters.
Inscription: ON 27TH NOVEMBER 1943 AT 02:15/ LANCASTER BOMBER ED393 VN-K/CRASHED NEAR THIS SPOT./ AIRBORNE FROM SKELLINGTHORPE FOR BERLIN AT 17:08/ BUT DIVERTED ON ITS RETURN DUE TO FOG,/ FIRST TO MELBOURNE AND THEN POCKLINGTON/ BEFORE RUNNING OUT OF FUEL, STRIKING TREES, A FARMHOUSE/ AND CRASHING INTO INGS HOUSE./ (names)/ DEDICATED TO THEIR MEMORY BY/ HH 'CHARLIE' ROSS/ WITNESS AND SON OF ONE OF THE RESCUERS
Location: Canal Head picnic area Off York Road (A1079 Pocklington East Yorkshire Antrim YO42 1NW England
Grid Ref: SE 79980 47340
Coordinates: 53.916043339688,-0.783782294012

The aircraft diverted from fog-bound Lincolnshire to Yorkshire on return from Berlin, lost height in landing circuit and crashed at Canal Head, Pocklington, destroying the Canal Head public house and cottages on Ramsdale Terrace.
